subject: Post-call: RAG config & eval playbook — next steps for AegisPharma
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Ng <samantha.ng@aegispharma.com>, Carlos Ruiz <c.ruiz@aegispharma.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Oct 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: RAG config & eval playbook — next steps for AegisPharma

Hi Samantha / Carlos,

Thanks again for the time today — appreciate the clear rundown of AegisPharma's use cases (regulatory Q&A, SOP search, and line-of-business triage). As promised, a compact recap of what we recommend for an initial pilot plus the concrete next steps: 

Summary recommendations (pilot scope):
- Retrieval: dense embeddings store with 2x shard replicas, chunking at ~400 tokens (overlap 40 tokens) for SOPs and regulatory docs.
- Retriever model: semantic embeddings using "redwood-embed-small-v1" for cost/latency tradeoff; optionally "redwood-embed-2x" for higher-recall collections.
- Reranker: cross-encoder reranker (distilroberta-cross-encoder) for top-10 rerank step; fallback to lightweight scoring for memory-limited infra.
- LLMs for response generation: start with Redwood-Text-2-7B (q4f16) for throughput; keep a canary Redwood-Text-6B variant for higher-quality checks.
- Grounding metrics to track: precision@1, MRR@5, grounding-fraction (answers with verifiable citations), and an automated hallucination-rate estimate on our QA seed.

Deliverables we agreed to share:
- A reproducible prompt set (seed examples) + evaluation harness (attached: aegis_prompt_set_v1.jsonl).
- A small benchmark run (CSV) with retrieval + reranker configs (attached: aegis_rag_benchmark_v1.csv).
- A short playbook with recommended runtime settings and config templates (attached PDF).

Next steps / asks (by priority):
1) You: confirm the list of source collections (SOPs, regulatory binders, training logs) and whether PHI is present in any.
2) Redwood: we'll run a focused 3-day eval (repro run) across 3 retrieval configs and share MRR/precision slices and example failure cases.
3) Schedule a 30-min tech sync (we proposed Tue morning) to walk retrieval parameters and access for a read-only S3/Drive dump.

Quick note on regression risk: we'll include a small set of production prompts you shared and run continuous quality checks against them once serving runs begin. If we see a >5% drop in grounding precision for top-1, we'll flag and propose a rollback to the canary model.

I've attached the artifacts and a Google Drive link to the benchmark run above. Laura will pick up the perf/ops side and Dylan will own the reranker experiments.

Thanks — Ben

--
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | (415) 555-0123

Thanks Ben — this is really clear and helpful. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Sources: SOPs (all regions), Regulatory binders (US + EU), and a small set of anonymized clinical logs (no direct PHI in the subset we'll share).
2) Our preference is to prioritize precision@1 for the SOP use case — a false instruction is high risk.
3) We're okay with Redwood running the 3-day eval; we'll provision read-only S3 access early next week.

A couple of asks back to you: can you include an explicit MRR@5 vs latency table for the two embedding models you mentioned? Also, for the reranker, do you have a rough per-request latency estimate (CPU vs GPU) for the cross-encoder on our expected query volumes (~120 QPS burst)?

Let's tentatively move the tech sync to Tue 10/6 10:00am PT — does that work for Laura and Dylan?

--
Samantha Ng

Subject: Re: Post-call: RAG config & eval playbook — next steps for AegisPharma

Great — thanks for the confirmations, Samantha. Quick answers below and a short plan for Tuesday's sync.

Answers to asks:
- MRR@5 vs latency table: attached in the CSV; short summary: redwood-embed-small-v1 gives median retrieval latency ~28ms and MRR@5 0.62 on the seed; redwood-embed-2x gives median retrieval latency ~46ms and MRR@5 0.71 (see CSV drive link).
- Reranker latency: distilroberta cross-encoder (CPU optimized) averages ~42ms per pair on our c5d-like instance for top-10 scoring; GPU batched runs (T4 equivalent) push that down to ~8-12ms per pair with batching. For 120 QPS burst, we'd recommend running the reranker on GPUs with batching (target P99 latency budget for the whole pipeline ~400ms).

Proposed agenda Tue 10/6 10:00am PT (30 mins):
- 5 min: goals & success criteria (precision@1 target)
- 10 min: retrieval config choices (chunk size, overlap, embedding model)
- 10 min: reranker tradeoffs + latency/cost options (GPU vs CPU)
- 5 min: access & next deliverables (S3 read-only + sample manifest)

Prep items for the call (we'll bring these):
- Short slide with MRR/latency tradeoffs (we'll share live)
- Live demo of reranker on 10 sample queries (Dylan)
- A small failure-case set from the CSV (Laura)

If that agenda looks good we'll lock the calendar invite (sending now). Also attaching a lightweight ops checklist in the PDF for your infra team to review ahead of time.

Ben
